vcu_0159_08002f08.name: vcu_serial_match_set_flag
vcu_0159_08002f08.summary: Compare two 14-byte strings and set a flag when they are identical
vcu_0159_08002f08.description: Compares param_1 and param_2 byte by byte over exactly 14 bytes (index kept in a u8 loop counter, stops at the first difference). If all 14 bytes match, writes 1 to the global flag DAT_20001f68; otherwise the flag is left untouched (it is never cleared here). The 14-byte length matches the 14-character product/serial string handled by vcu_serial_check_default and vcu_serial_parse_variant_code, so this is most likely a serial-number-equals-stored-copy check. Called from the large configuration/communication routine vcu_0159_08009da8.

returns.description: nothing; result is the side effect on DAT_20001f68

vcu_0159_08002f08.notes: That the buffers are serial numbers is inferred from the length 14 and the caller, not proven.

vcu_0159_0800332c.name: vcu_debounce_condition_a
vcu_0159_0800332c.summary: Up/down debounce counter (limit 20) that drives the output flag DAT_20001f69
vcu_0159_0800332c.description: Part of a family of small per-tick condition/flag helpers (see vcu_condition_b_latch_flags) called from the main loop handlers. When DAT_20001b62 < 10 (likely a speed value), bit0 of status word DAT_20001f78 is clear and bit3 of DAT_20001f78 or of DAT_20001e6a is set, the saturating counter DAT_20001880 is incremented; once it has reached 0x14 (20 calls) DAT_20001f69 is set to 1. Otherwise, when bit3 of DAT_20001f78 or bit3 of DAT_20001e6a is clear, the counter is decremented and DAT_20001f69 is cleared when it is already 0. This gives hysteresis so the flag only changes after about 20 consecutive calls.
vcu_0159_0800332c.notes: Meaning of the status bits (f78 bit0/bit3, e6a bit3) and of b62 as speed is unknown; the decompiled OR/AND mixture of the bit tests is reproduced literally.

vcu_0159_0800339c.name: vcu_condition_b_latch_flags
vcu_0159_0800339c.summary: Set or clear flag bit 2 of DAT_20001aec and DAT_20001875 from status bits
vcu_0159_0800339c.description: Companion of vcu_debounce_condition_a. If bit6 of DAT_20001e68 is set, DAT_20001b62 < 10, bit0 of DAT_20001f78 is clear and bit3 of DAT_20001e6a is set, it ORs 4 into the flag word DAT_20001aec and sets DAT_20001875 to 1. If instead bit6 of e68 is clear or bit3 of e6a is clear it clears bit 2 of aec (AND 0xFFFB) and clears DAT_20001875. In all other cases the state is left unchanged (latching behaviour). No counter is involved, so the change is immediate.
vcu_0159_0800339c.notes: Semantics of the individual bits are not known.

vcu_0159_08003400.name: vcu_periodic_100_tick_check
vcu_0159_08003400.summary: Every 100 calls of the counter DAT_2000102c, raise DAT_20001fc0 if conditions hold
vcu_0159_08003400.description: DAT_2000102c is a free-running tick counter incremented elsewhere (the access is flagged as address-taken/RW). When it reaches 100 it is reset to 0 and, if bit6 of DAT_20001e68 and bit4 of DAT_20001af2 are both set, or DAT_2000123e equals 6, the request flag DAT_20001fc0 is set to 1 (consumed elsewhere). Below 100 nothing happens. Acts as a 100-period timed event generator.
vcu_0159_08003400.notes: Tick period (and whether 0x123e is a state/mode byte) not determined.

vcu_0159_08003b00.name: vcu_event_countdown_a
vcu_0159_08003b00.summary: Countdown timer reloaded on input change; sets DAT_20001fb4 on expiry
vcu_0159_08003b00.description: One of a group of countdown helpers (see vcu_event_countdown_b). If DAT_20001f48 is 0 and DAT_20001b62 < 30: when DAT_200021b5 == 3 it sets DAT_20001fb4 = 1; when the event latch DAT_20001fbc differs from the remembered copy DAT_2000134c, it copies it into 134c, clears fbc and reloads the countdown DAT_20001fac with param_1. A nonzero countdown is decremented each call and when it reaches 0 sets DAT_20001fb4 = 1. If the guard fails, the countdown is zeroed and DAT_200021b5 is cleared if it was 3. At the end a pending latch value of 1 in fbc is cleared. param_1 is the timeout in calls.
vcu_0159_08003b00.notes: DAT_20001fbc looks like a shared change/event latch (button or input edge) but its source is unknown.

vcu_0159_08003b74.name: vcu_event_countdown_b
vcu_0159_08003b74.summary: Countdown timer reloaded on event latch change; sets DAT_20001fd4 at expiry
vcu_0159_08003b74.description: Sibling of vcu_event_countdown_a. When the latch DAT_20001fbc differs from the stored copy DAT_2000134d it copies it, clears the latch, reloads the 16-bit countdown DAT_20001fd2 with param_1 and, if DAT_20001fd4 was 1, clears DAT_20001fd4 and DAT_200021b8. Then, while the countdown is nonzero it decrements it and sets DAT_20001fd4 = 1 when it reaches 0; if it is already 0 it re-arms it with param_1. Effectively a repeating timer whose expiry flag is DAT_20001fd4.
vcu_0159_08003b74.notes: Purpose of DAT_200021b8 and the consumer of fd4 not identified.

vcu_0159_08003bc8.name: vcu_deferred_system_reset
vcu_0159_08003bc8.summary: After 20 calls with DAT_20001f52 == 1, trigger a Cortex-M system reset
vcu_0159_08003bc8.description: If the request byte DAT_20001f52 equals 1, increments the counter DAT_2000134e; once it exceeds 0x13 (i.e. on the 20th call) it executes a DSB, writes SCB->AIRCR (0xE000ED0C) with VECTKEY 0x5FA and SYSRESETREQ (bit 2) while preserving PRIGROUP (mask 0x700), executes another DSB and spins forever until the reset occurs. This is the CMSIS NVIC_SystemReset() sequence preceded by a debounce delay. Used to restart the VCU (e.g. after a configuration/update command); called from the main handler vcu_0159_0800a1d0.

returns.description: does not return once the reset condition is met

vcu_0159_08003bc8.notes: The counter is not cleared when DAT_20001f52 is not 1, so non-consecutive requests also accumulate.

vcu_0159_08003bf0.name: vcu_cycle_mode_on_request
vcu_0159_08003bf0.summary: On a request flag, step a 3-state selector and map it to DAT_20001b94
vcu_0159_08003bf0.description: When the request flag DAT_20001f75 is nonzero it is cleared and the selector DAT_2000135c (0,1,2) is mapped to the output DAT_20001b94 as 0 -> 2, 1 -> 1, 2 -> 0, then the selector is incremented and wrapped back to 0 after 2. So each request cycles through three values, in the order 2, 1, 0 for the output. Looks like a three-level setting (e.g. riding/speed mode or light level) toggled by a button press; called from the main handlers vcu_0159_0800a15c and 0800a1d0.
vcu_0159_08003bf0.notes: What DAT_20001b94 controls (speed mode / light level) is unverified.

vcu_0159_08004714.name: vcu_serial_parse_variant_code
vcu_0159_08004714.summary: Decode the variant letter of a '1K1x' serial prefix into DAT_20001fa7
vcu_0159_08004714.description: param_1 points to a character string. If it begins with "1K1", the 4th character is mapped to a variant index stored in DAT_20001fa7: 'A'->0, 'E'->1, 'D'->2, 'U'->3, 'Z'->4, 'I'->5, 'G'->6, anything else -> 1. If the prefix is not "1K1" the index is 4. It then sets DAT_20001fa5 = 1 (variant valid/changed) and stores ((DAT_20001b40 >> 8) + 3) & 0xFF into DAT_20001032. The index is consumed by vcu_apply_variant_config to select the feature flag words; both are called from vcu_0159_08009da8.

params.name: param_1
params.description: pointer to the serial/model string (at least 4 chars)

returns.description: nothing; results in DAT_20001fa7, DAT_20001fa5, DAT_20001032

vcu_0159_08004714.notes: The letters are likely market/region or model variants; exact meaning is a guess. The role of DAT_20001b40>>8 (+3) is unknown.

vcu_0159_08004f74.name: vcu_toggle_special_mode
vcu_0159_08004f74.summary: Toggle mode byte DAT_20001fa4 between its current value and the special value 4
vcu_0159_08004f74.description: Active only when bit4 of DAT_20001aee is set and the request flag DAT_20001f72 is nonzero; the flag is consumed (cleared). If the mode DAT_20001fa4 is already 4, it is restored from the saved value DAT_20001354. Otherwise, if DAT_20001b62 < 0x32, the current mode is saved in DAT_20001354 and DAT_20001fa4 is set to 4. Called from the main handlers (vcu_0159_0800a15c, 0800a1d0).
vcu_0159_08004f74.notes: DAT_20001b62 < 50 is a gate, probably a speed limit in some unit; meaning of mode 4 unknown.

vcu_0159_08005380.name: vcu_error_code_clear_if_current
vcu_0159_08005380.summary: Clear the active error code DAT_2000123c when it equals the given code
vcu_0159_08005380.description: If the currently displayed/active error code DAT_2000123c equals param_1 it is set to 0. Does not touch the error bitmap (vcu_error_code_clear does that). Called from vcu_0159_080029d0 and vcu_0159_08003f40.
vcu_0159_08005380.notes: Interpretation of DAT_2000123c as an error code is inferred from the sibling functions with 48-bit bitmaps.

vcu_0159_08005394.name: vcu_error_code_clear
vcu_0159_08005394.summary: Clear error code from active slot and bit i-1 of the 48-bit error bitmap
vcu_0159_08005394.description: First clears the active error code DAT_2000123c if it equals param_1. Then for codes 1..48 (param_1 != 0 and < 0x31) clears bit (param_1-1) in a 48-bit pending-error set spread over three u16 words: bits 0-15 in DAT_20001ce0, 16-31 in DAT_20001ce2 and 32-47 in DAT_20001ce4. Out-of-range codes only affect the active slot. Paired with vcu_warning_code_clear which does the same for codes 10..57 in DAT_20001cd8..cde and DAT_2000123d; reset together by vcu_error_state_reset. Callers: vcu_0159_08002d18, vcu_0159_08003f40.

params.name: param_1
params.description: error code, 1..48 (0 and larger values ignored for the bitmap)

vcu_0159_08005394.notes: Which of the two bitmap groups is 'error' versus 'warning' is a guess; both are fault-code sets.

vcu_0159_080053ec.name: vcu_error_state_reset
vcu_0159_080053ec.summary: Zero the active error code, DAT_20001b66 and the 3-word error bitmap
vcu_0159_080053ec.description: Writes 0 to DAT_2000123c (active code), DAT_20001b66 and the three bitmap words DAT_20001ce0, DAT_20001ce2 and DAT_20001ce4 used by vcu_error_code_clear. Called from vcu_0159_0800a39c together with vcu_warning_state_reset, vcu_aux_flags_reset and the other clear helpers, i.e. a global reset of fault state.
vcu_0159_080053ec.notes: DAT_20001b66 is probably a mirror of the active error code or a count; unknown.

vcu_0159_08005410.name: vcu_warning_state_reset
vcu_0159_08005410.summary: Zero the active warning code, DAT_20001b64 and the 4-word warning bitmap
vcu_0159_08005410.description: Writes 0 to DAT_2000123d (active code), DAT_20001b64 and the four u16 bitmap words DAT_20001cd8, cda, cdc and cde used by vcu_warning_code_clear. Called from vcu_0159_0800a39c together with vcu_error_state_reset.
vcu_0159_08005410.notes: Error vs warning naming is a guess.

vcu_0159_08005434.name: vcu_warning_code_clear
vcu_0159_08005434.summary: Clear warning code from active slot and bit (code-10) of the warning bitmap
vcu_0159_08005434.description: Clears the active code DAT_2000123d if it equals param_1. For codes 10..57 (9 < param_1 < 0x3a) the bit index idx = param_1 - 10 is cleared in a bitmap of u16 words: idx 0-15 in DAT_20001cd8, 16-31 in cda, 32-47 in cdc, 48-63 in cde (the last word is reachable only for idx >= 48, which the range check prevents, so it is effectively dead). Sibling of vcu_error_code_clear with a different code range and storage. Callers: vcu_0159_08003f40, vcu_0159_0800a500.
vcu_0159_08005434.notes: Code range 10..57 suggests the warning numbering is offset from the error numbering; unverified.

vcu_0159_080054a4.name: vcu_clear_flag_bits_9_11
vcu_0159_080054a4.summary: Clear bits 9..11 of the 16-bit flag word DAT_20001f98
vcu_0159_080054a4.description: Performs DAT_20001f98 &= 0xF1FF, clearing the three-bit field at bits 9-11. Part of the group of clear/reset helpers called together from vcu_0159_0800a39c. DAT_20001f8c is address-taken nearby so f98 is probably a member of a status structure.

vcu_0159_080054b4.name: vcu_aux_flags_reset
vcu_0159_080054b4.description: Stores 0 to DAT_20002028, DAT_20002023, DAT_20002022, DAT_200021be and DAT_200021bb in that order. Called only from vcu_0159_0800a39c alongside vcu_error_state_reset and vcu_warning_state_reset, so it is a state-clear helper of the same reset event.
vcu_0159_080054b4.notes: Meaning of the five variables is unknown.

vcu_0159_080054d0.name: vcu_frame_checksum
vcu_0159_080054d0.summary: Ones'-complement of the 16-bit sum of bytes (Ninebot-style frame checksum)
vcu_0159_080054d0.description: Sums param_2 bytes starting at param_1 into a 16-bit accumulator (wraparound) and returns the bitwise NOT of the sum. This is the typical Ninebot/Xiaomi frame checksum (0xFFFF ^ sum). Called from vcu_0159_08008a9e, a frame build/verify routine. The result is returned as a ushort, low byte then high byte presumably appended to the frame.
vcu_0159_080054d0.notes: Which bytes of the frame (e.g. length..data) are included is decided by the caller.

vcu_14f_080055d0.name: DebugMon_Handler
vcu_14f_080055d0.summary: Debug monitor exception handler: empty, returns immediately
vcu_14f_080055d0.description: Cortex-M DebugMonitor exception vector (vector 12). The handler is a single return instruction, so debug monitor events are ignored. Present only in the older builds 148..14f.

vcu_14f_080056d4.name: EXINT0_IRQHandler
vcu_14f_080056d4.summary: EXINT line 0 interrupt handler: empty stub
vcu_14f_080056d4.description: Vector for external interrupt line 0 (EXINT0). The body is a single return and does not clear the EXINT pending bit, so the interrupt is evidently not enabled in practice. Present only in builds 148..14f.

vcu_14f_08005740.name: EXINT9_5_IRQHandler
vcu_14f_08005740.summary: EXINT lines 9..5 shared interrupt handler: empty stub
vcu_14f_08005740.description: Vector for the shared external interrupt of EXINT lines 5-9. The body is a single return and does not clear any pending flag, so it is a placeholder for an unused interrupt. Present only in builds 148..14f.

vcu_0159_08005914.name: vcu_sum_s16_minus_trailer
vcu_0159_08005914.summary: Sum an array of s16 and subtract the two s16 words at index 250 and 251
vcu_0159_08005914.description: Adds up the first param_2 signed 16-bit values of the array at param_1 and returns that sum minus the s16 at byte offset 500 (index 250) and minus the s16 at byte offset 0x1F6 (index 251). It looks like a block integrity check: a 512-byte block of 16-bit words whose last words hold stored check values, the return being 0 when valid. Callers vcu_0159_08005bb4 and vcu_0159_08007d88, which also use vcu_flash_page_count and vcu_copy_bytes_src_dst, so this belongs to the stored-parameter/firmware-image handling code.

returns.description: sum minus trailer words; 0 expected when consistent

vcu_0159_08005914.notes: Whether param_2 includes the two trailer words (e.g. 250 vs 252) is decided by callers; purpose is inferred.

vcu_0159_08005b2c.name: vcu_flash_page_count
vcu_0159_08005b2c.summary: Ceiling division of a byte count by 1024
vcu_0159_08005b2c.description: Returns param_1 >> 10, plus 1 if any of the low 10 bits are set, i.e. ceil(param_1 / 1024). 1 KiB is the AT32F415 flash erase page size, so this converts an image length to the number of pages to erase/program. Called from vcu_0159_08005b40.

vcu_0159_08005b7e.name: vcu_copy_bytes_src_dst
vcu_0159_08005b7e.summary: Byte-wise copy of param_3 bytes from param_1 to param_2
vcu_0159_08005b7e.description: Simple forward byte loop copying from src (param_1) to dst (param_2). Note the argument order is source first, unlike memcpy. No overlap handling. Called from vcu_0159_08005bb4, 080060b8 and 08009da8.

vcu_0159_08005d9a.name: HardFault_Handler
vcu_0159_08005d9a.description: Cortex-M HardFault vector. Spins forever; the watchdog (if running) will reset the device, otherwise the MCU hangs. No fault status is saved.

vcu_0159_08005db8.name: vcu_apply_variant_config
vcu_0159_08005db8.summary: Build four 16-bit option words from the variant index DAT_20001fa7 and publish them
vcu_0159_08005db8.description: Starts from default values (DAT_20001034 = 0x279F, DAT_20001036 = 0xA5A1, DAT_20001038 base 0x83DD, DAT_2000103a with bits 4-5 cleared and bit 1 set) and switches on the variant index DAT_20001fa7 (set by vcu_serial_parse_variant_code, values 0..6, default for other values) to override bit fields in these four words and, for cases 1, 2, 5 and default, to clear bit 12 of DAT_20001aee (case 2 also sets bit 11). Finally the words are copied into the output/shadow words DAT_20001aea, DAT_20001b14, DAT_20001b16 and DAT_20001b18 (4 x u16 = 8 bytes, likely a feature/option mask sent in a protocol frame). Cases 4 and 6 share one configuration, case 3 keeps the defaults. Called from vcu_0159_08009da8 and vcu_0159_0800b294.
vcu_0159_08005db8.notes: Meaning of the individual bits of the four words is unknown; they could be feature enables per model/market variant.

vcu_153_08006490.name: vcu_tea_decrypt_block
vcu_153_08006490.summary: TEA decryption of one 64-bit block with a 128-bit key (32 rounds)
vcu_153_08006490.description: Tiny Encryption Algorithm decrypt: v0 = param_1[0], v1 = param_1[1], sum starts at 0xC6EF3720 (= 32 * delta, delta 0x9E3779B9; the code adds 0x61C88647 each round, i.e. subtracts delta). Each of 32 rounds does v1 -= ((v0<<4)+k[2]) ^ (v0+sum) ^ ((v0>>5)+k[3]) then v0 -= ((v1<<4)+k[0]) ^ (v1+sum) ^ ((v1>>5)+k[1]). The result is written back in place. No direct callers in the image (called indirectly or the call was optimised away); not present in the 0159 build.

params.name: param_1
params.description: pointer to two u32 words (the 8-byte block, decrypted in place)

params.name: param_2
params.description: pointer to four u32 key words

vcu_153_08006490.notes: Plain TEA (not XTEA): the key index is fixed per half-round, no key schedule on sum. What data it protects is not known from this function.

vcu_0159_080066dc.name: vcu_serial_check_default
vcu_0159_080066dc.summary: Classify the stored serial string at DAT_20001ad4 against the default '1K1E0000000001'
vcu_0159_080066dc.description: Builds the 14-character template "1K1E0000000001" on the stack and compares it with the string at DAT_20001ad4, character by character. Returns 1 if all 14 characters match (factory default / unprogrammed serial), 2 if a non-alphanumeric character (not 0-9, A-Z, a-z) is found before 14 characters were matched (invalid serial), and 0 if an alphanumeric character differs from the template (a real, different serial). Called from vcu_0159_08005bb4.

returns.description: 0 = different valid serial, 1 = equals default template, 2 = invalid (non-alphanumeric) character

vcu_0159_080066dc.notes: Role of the string as a serial number follows from its '1K1' prefix and the sibling parser; return code meanings derived from control flow.

vcu_14f_08006710.name: vcu_latch_event_flags_a
vcu_14f_08006710.summary: One-shot: set bit0 then bit1 of DAT_20001a7a, setting bit 11 of DAT_20001a38/20001a36
vcu_14f_08006710.description: If bit0 of the latch byte DAT_20001a7a is clear it sets it and ORs 0x800 into the flag word DAT_20001a38; if bit1 is clear it sets it and ORs 0x800 into DAT_20001a36. So each flag word gets bit 11 set exactly once, guarded by a latch. The duplicated test in the decompilation is an artifact of an atomic/exclusive access. Older-build (148..14f) counterpart of vcu_latch_event_flags_b; no direct callers (invoked indirectly).
vcu_14f_08006710.notes: The meaning of bit 11 of these words is unknown.

vcu_0159_08006814.name: vcu_count_nonzero_nibbles
vcu_0159_08006814.summary: Count how many of the 8 nibbles of a u32 are nonzero
vcu_0159_08006814.description: Iterates over the 8 hexadecimal digits of param_1 (shift right by 4 each time) and increments a counter for each nibble not equal to 0. Returns the count (0..8). Called from vcu_0159_08007a48.

vcu_0159_0800686c.name: vcu_sanitize_mode_1_to_4
vcu_0159_0800686c.summary: Force the byte at param_1 into the range 1..4 (default 1)
vcu_0159_0800686c.description: If *param_1 is not one of 1, 2, 3 or 4, it is replaced by 1. Used to validate a 4-valued setting loaded from stored configuration. Called from vcu_0159_08009da8.

params.name: param_1
params.description: pointer to the u8 setting to validate

vcu_0159_0800691c.name: vcu_latch_event_flags_b
vcu_0159_0800691c.summary: One-shot: set bits 0..2 of DAT_20001b32 and the matching flags in aee/af0/b12
vcu_0159_0800691c.description: Three independent latches in DAT_20001b32. If bit0 is clear it sets it and ORs 0x800 into DAT_20001af0; if bit1 is clear it sets it and ORs 0x800 into DAT_20001aee; if bit2 is clear it sets it and ORs 2 into DAT_20001b12. The duplicate tests are decompiler artifacts. Newer-build (152/153/0159) version of vcu_latch_event_flags_a with an additional third latch. Called from vcu_0159_0800d858.
vcu_0159_0800691c.notes: The meaning of the flag bits is unknown; it might be a one-time announcement/feature-present flag.

vcu_0159_08006990.name: MemManage_Handler
vcu_0159_08006990.description: Cortex-M MemManage exception vector. Spins forever without saving fault status.

vcu_0159_080069b0.name: NMI_Handler
vcu_0159_080069b0.summary: NMI exception handler: empty, returns immediately
vcu_0159_080069b0.description: Cortex-M Non-Maskable Interrupt vector. Single return instruction; NMI events (e.g. clock failure detect) are ignored.

vcu_0159_08006b00.name: vcu_digits4_to_int
vcu_0159_08006b00.summary: Convert four decimal-digit bytes (d0 d1 d2 d3) to a 4-digit integer
vcu_0159_08006b00.description: Computes ((d0*10 + d1)*10 + d2)*10 + d3 from param_1[0..3], with no subtraction of '0', so the bytes are raw digit values 0..9 (not ASCII), and returns the result sign-extended from 16 bits. Called from vcu_0159_080069b4.

params.name: param_1
params.description: pointer to 4 digit bytes, most significant first

vcu_0159_08007ab4.name: PendSV_Handler
vcu_0159_08007ab4.summary: PendSV exception handler: empty, returns immediately
vcu_0159_08007ab4.description: Cortex-M PendSV vector. A single return instruction; the firmware does not use an RTOS context switch through PendSV.
